newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were seen opening higher Thursday, in line with LME copper, as the market bounced back from Wednesday's sharp slide.
COMEX September copper was seen opening up 0.50 to 1.00 cents from Wednesday's close at 102.50 cents a pound, after trading between 102.65 and 105.30 cents in overnight ACCESS trade.
LME copper stocks rose 2,000 tonnes to 136,325 tonnes in Thursday's data, while COMEX copper stocks fell 1,699 short tons to 38,023 short tons Wednesday.

In industry news, Sterlite Industrial's 100,000 tonnes a year copper smelter in India remains shut down since Sunday due to suspected gas leak, while activity at the Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal was also suspended for the third day due to a strike.
But the seasonal summer demand slowdown meant the market was ignoring any supply problems, traders said.
